Looking at the validator error: the previous attempt emitted the **Markdown embed** (image + source footer) instead of the actual `.fd` source content. The task asks for the FigDown document itself — that's what needs the `figdown 0.1 <genre>` first line, node/edge declarations, etc. Below is the corrected `.fd` source (topology genre, since this is a network topology of switches, a router, and two upstream hubs — nodes/links with roles and diverse paths, not a table or block diagram).

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

node access1 "access1"
node access2 "access2"
node branch "branch"
node hubprimary "hubprimary"
node hubbackup "hubbackup"

link access1 branch
link access2 branch
link branch hubprimary "primary"
link branch hubbackup "backup"
```

To embed this in a host Markdown document once built and validated:

```markdown
![Branch office WAN uplinks](figures/branch-wan-uplinks.svg)

<sub>source: [figures/branch-wan-uplinks.fd](figures/branch-wan-uplinks.fd)</sub>
```

Notes:
- The five nodes and four links match exactly what the description specifies: `access1`–`branch`, `access2`–`branch`, `branch`–`hubprimary`, `branch`–`hubbackup`.
- The primary/backup distinction is carried as link labels (`"primary"` / `"backup"`) rather than colour alone, per the rule that meaning must survive in text, not paint.
- I did not have `reference/experimental/topology.md` open in this session to confirm its exact preferred keyword spellings (e.g., whether it ranks `node`/`link` against more specific alternates). Before this file is treated as final, run `node <skill-dir>/build-svg.js branch-wan-uplinks.fd` and fix any `Line N:` errors it reports against that genre file's actual vocabulary.
